title: Karna's abandonment
hook: at the princes' tournament a stranger walks into the arena and matches Arjuna, and one woman in the stands knows him

segments.voice: Yesterday, a stranger asked for the armor, and Karna cut it from his body. He gives because someone asked.

Yesterday's scene came from further down the road; today we're back in the order of events, and Karna still wears his armor. A great arena in Hastinapura. Drona, the princes' teacher, has arranged a day for them to show the city what they've learned. The stands are packed, Kunti among the women. The cousins ride and fight and shoot, and Arjuna outshines them all, the text says, while the crowd roars. Then a sound at the gate. Someone new walks in.
screen: `A DAY TO SHOW THEIR SKILL.` → `ARJUNA OUTSHINES THEM ALL.` → `A SOUND AT THE GATE.`

segments.voice: It's Karna, tall and shining, in his armor and earrings. He barely bows to the teachers. He turns to Arjuna and says, in effect: everything you've done, I'll do. And he does, one feat after another, while the crowd stares. Duryodhana is overjoyed. Here at last is someone to match the brother he resents, and he embraces Karna like a friend. Then Karna asks to fight Arjuna, one against one. And now the story swings up into the stands. Kunti sees the armor and the earrings, and she knows. This is her son, the boy she set on the river, about to fight another of her sons. The text says she faints. Vidura has her revived with cool water and sandal paste, and she comes to and watches, unable to say a word. Everyone else in the stands sees two rivals. One person sees two brothers, and she can't tell anyone. The abandonment wasn't only something that happened long ago by a river. It's still happening, in the silence of a mother in a crowd. Karna doesn't know. Arjuna doesn't know. Only Kunti does, and us, the listeners. Every word spoken in that arena now means two things.
screen: `KARNA MATCHES ARJUNA.` · `DURYODHANA EMBRACES HIM.` · `KUNTI KNOWS, AND FAINTS.` · `TWO RIVALS, OR TWO BROTHERS.` · then, large: `SHE CAN'T TELL ANYONE.`

segments.voice: Call up a crowd you were part of recently: a meeting, a game, a family gathering. Bring to mind one face from it, and wonder, without guessing, what they might have been carrying that nobody else could see. Let that wondering soften how you see them.
Karna's abandonment. A stranger matches Arjuna in the arena, and in the stands, the mother who set him adrift knows him, and keeps silent.
Your line: she can't tell anyone. Two rivals in the arena, two brothers in her eyes. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: The tournament scene, with Karna's entrance and Kunti's fainting, is retold by Mahabharata storytellers and on stage, where it lets the audience see what the characters can't.

original.note: Sanskrit karṇa: the name the world knows him by; he is also called Vasusena and Radheya.

trapdoor: what you thought: a rival shows up to challenge the hero.
what it means: a brother challenges a brother, and only their mother knows.
what a scholar hears: the listener shares Kunti's secret, so every exchange in the arena carries a meaning the fighters can't hear.

chat.says: Why did Kunti faint at the tournament?
options: She saw the armor and earrings and knew the newcomer was her own son.
She feared Arjuna would be hurt by a stranger she'd never seen.
The crowd was so loud and hot that she was overcome by the heat.
chat.meaning: Kunti recognized Karna by his armor and earrings: the son she set on the river, about to fight Arjuna. She couldn't say a word.

Arjuna.meaning: Pandu's third son, the archer, son of Indra

Vidura.meaning: the maid's son, wise in dharma, uncle to the cousins

recall: the serpent people below the waters
